newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gets Chinese assurance on jailed dissident.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gets Chinese assurance on jailed dissident.

text.p: China assured the United States on Friday it was taking no further punitive action against its best-known dissident after Secretary of State Madeleine Albright voiced concern, the State Department said.

The U.S. Embassy in Beijing contacted the Foreign Ministry three times on Friday to express Albright's personal concern and to seek information about the condition of the dissident, Wei Jingsheng, department spokesman John Dinger said.

"The Foreign Ministry responded with an account of an altercation between Wei and another inmate and added that Wei was criticised by prison authorities but no other action was being taken against Wei," Dinger said.

Accounts reaching Washington had said fellow prisoners severely beat Wei after being promised reduced sentences if they attacked him. Wei, 47, is serving a 14-year sentence for subversion at a prison in the northern province of Hebei.

In Beijing a relative who visited Wei in mid-June told Reuters electricity to Wei's cell was cut off and he had been banned from shopping at the prison canteen. The State Department said it had no independent information.
"The bottom line about it is that we believe that Wei and all others imprisoned for peacefully expressing political rights should be released," Dinger said.

House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Friday condemned the reported prison camp beating of Wei and urged Albright to instruct U.S. Ambassador James Sasser to request a visit with him immediately to provide medical assistance.
"We cannot stand by while the Chinese government slowly destroys this proud and courageous man," the Georgia Republican said in a letter to Albright.
